{{Term/Store|Navi||Series, OoT, OoT3D, MM, MM3D, OoT (Himekawa)}} is a recurring character in {{TLoZ Series}}.<ref>{{Cite Book|quote= |book= E |publisher= |page= 239 {{Exp Game|OoT}}}}</ref><ref name="HH 110">{{Cite Book|quote= Link set off on his horse, Epona, who lived at Lon Lon Ranch. Months passed as he wandered in search of his companion, Navi, eventually losing himself in a mysterious forest. It just so happened that this forest led to a parallel world known as Termina.|book= HH |publisher= |page= 110 {{Exp Game|MM}}}}</ref><ref name="OoT (Himekawa) 20">{{Cite Book|quote= ...The boy without a fairy... Bring him to me. Go, Navi! |character= [[Deku Tree]] |book= OoT (Himekawa) |volume= 1 |publisher= |page= 20}}</ref>{{Name Ref|LatPoD, MM (Himekawa), HW}} She is a [[Fairy]] who serves as [[Link]]'s companion in his quest to save [[Hyrule]].<ref name="Partner">{{Cite|I'm {{Color OoT3D|White|Navi}} the fairy! The Great Deku Tree asked me to be your {{Color OoT3D|White|partner}} from now on! Nice to meet you!|Navi|OoT3D}}</ref>

==Biography==
==={{OoT|-}}===
Since Link is not a [[Kokiri]] and does not have a Fairy to call his own, Navi is summoned by the [[Great Deku Tree]] to accompany him on his quest to save [[Hyrule]].<ref name="Partner"/><ref name="Navi">{{Cite|Navi the fairy... Thou must aid Link... And Link... When {{Color OoT3D|Light Blue|Navi}} speaks, use {{Icon|OoT3D Navi}} to listen well to her words of wisdom...|Great Deku Tree|OoT3D}}</ref> Throughout the game, Navi provides Link with a variety of clues to help him solve puzzles and progress in his quest.<ref>{{Cite|Look at this wall! The vines growing on it give it a rough surface... Maybe you can climb it, Link!|Navi|OoT3D}}</ref><ref>{{Cite|Wow! Look at all those Bomb Flowers! Is there any way you can set them all off at once?|Navi|OoT}}</ref><ref>{{Cite|Should we believe what Sheik said and go to Kakariko Village?|Navi|OoT}}</ref> Navi also helps Link learn the controls in the game, teaching him how to open doors and how to push and pull blocks.<ref>{{Cite|You can open a {{Color OoT3D|White|door}} by standing in front of it and pressing {{Icon|OoT3D A}}. Pay attention to what the Action Icon says. That's the {{Color OoT3D|White|A Button icon}} on the upper screen!|Navi|OoT3D}}</ref><ref>{{Cite|Stand next to this {{Color OoT3D|White|block}} and grab hold of it with {{Icon|OoT3D A}}. While holding {{Icon|OoT3D A}}, you can push or pull it. If you stand next to the {{Color OoT3D|White|block}} and press {{Icon|OoT3D A}} while pressing {{Icon|OoT3D Circle Pad}} towards the {{Color OoT3D|White|block}}, you can climb on top of it. Pay attention to what the {{Color OoT3D|White|Action Icon}} says!|Navi|OoT3D}}</ref> The player can listen to Navi's advice by pressing the C-Up Button in the controller whenever her name flashes on the screen.<ref name="Navi"/>

{{Frameless|[[File:Young Link Navi.png|thumb|170px|right|Link and Navi]]}}

Navi's primary purpose is to function as a focusing target. By pressing the Z Button, Navi targets the most nearby object, enemy, or person. She glows yellow to indicate when she is targeting an enemy, blue when Link can talk to someone from a distance, and green when she is targeting something of interest. Any time Navi targets something, she yells out to Link "Hey!", "Listen!", or "Watch out!" Pressing the C-Up Button while targeting an enemy allows Link to hear from Navi information about said foe. Once Link learns "[[Saria's Song]]," he can communicate with [[Saria]] through Navi.<ref>{{Cite|You want to talk to Saria, right? /Talk to Saria /No|Navi|OoT}}</ref> When Navi's help is not being used, she seemingly hides herself inside Link's hat. However, she can be summoned at any time by pressing the A Button while Link is standing still. In {{OoT3D}}, Navi also often tells Link to take a rest from playing.<ref>{{Cite Magazine/NP|quote= While Navi does sometimes give useful hints, more often then not she interrupts the game to repeatedly suggest that you take a break from playing.|issue= 268|date= June 2011|page= 82}}</ref>

Although Navi can target most enemies and give Link clues on how to defeat them, during the battle against [[Ganondorf]], Navi is unable to help him due to the waves of darkness produced by the King of Evil.<ref>{{Cite|Link! I can't help you! Because of the waves of darkness, I can't get close! I'm sorry, Link!|Navi|OoT}}</ref> Once Link defeats Ganondorf and escapes the crumbling [[Ganon's Castle]] along with [[Princess Zelda]], Navi apologizes for not having helped him in the battle.<ref>{{Cite|Link... I'm sorry I couldn't help you in the battle before!|Navi|OoT}}</ref> However, Ganondorf emerges shortly after from the castle ruins and transforms into Ganon. Navi, willing to aid Link, exclaims that she will not be held back by Ganondorf again and joins him in the fight, where they eventually defeat the King of Evil.<ref>{{Cite|There's no way he's going to hold me back again! This time, we fight together!|Navi|OoT}}</ref> After Princess Zelda sends Link back to his original time, Navi can be seen leaving Link's side for undisclosed reasons as she flies away into the lit window inside the [[Temple of Time]].

==={{MM|-}}===
During the prologue of {{MM}}, Link sets on a journey to find Navi after the events of {{OoT|-}}.<ref>{{Cite|Done with the battles he once waged across time, he embarked on a journey. A secret and personal journey... A journey in search of a beloved and invaluable friend... A friend with whom he parted ways when he finally fulfilled his heroic destiny and took his place among legends...|Prologue|MM}}</ref><ref name="HH 110"/>

==={{OoT|-}} (Himekawa)===
{{Noncanon|Start}}
Navi is first seen spying on [[Gohma]], as it begins feeding on the Great Deku Tree's insides. He tells her to go find Link,<ref name="OoT (Himekawa) 20"/> so she leads the boy to the Great Deku Tree, who is close to death. Once Link and [[Mido]] enter the Great Deku Tree's trunk, they are faced with Gohma. As Link battles the menace, Navi tells him about Gohma's week spot, its eye. <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= Link! Gohma's weakness is her eyeball! Aim for her eye!|book= OoT (Himekawa)|volume= 1|publisher= |page= 31}}</ref> Link then shoots the monster with his [[slingshot]], ending the battle. When Link realizes he is too late, the Great Deku Tree tells the boy he can defeat the evil growing in Hyrule. Navi is then commanded to help Link. <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= Navi... Help Link. I'm counting on you, too.|book= OoT (Himekawa)|volume= 1|publisher= |page= 36}}</ref> Throught the manga, Navi guides and accompanies Link, even comforting him when he worries about seeing [[Princess Zelda]] again. <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= You will! I'm sure she's somewhere safe. And she's been waiting for you the whole time! Play the ocarina Link. Maybe Princess Zelda will hear it!|book= OoT (Himekawa)|volume= 1|publisher= |page= 132}}</ref> As Link battles [[Ganondorf]], the Gerudo king uses his magic to keep Navi away. <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= L-Link! I can't get any closer! He's keeping me away with waves of darkness!|book= OoT (Himekawa)|volume= 2|publisher= |page= 78}}</ref> When he defeats the thief, Navi apologizes for not being able to help, <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= Link, I tried to help, but I couldn't...|book= OoT (Himekawa)|volume= 2|publisher= |page= 88}}</ref> but is reassured by Link that it's ok. <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= That's all right, Navi|book= OoT (Himekawa)|volume= 2|publisher= |page= 88}}</ref> Shockingly, Ganondorf is revealed to have survived the encounter, and transforms into the hideous beast [[Ganon]]. Link is wounded in the unexpected event, causing Navi to fret and worry. <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= Link. Snap out of it!|book= OoT (Himekawa)|volume= 2|publisher= |page= 94}}</ref> When Ganon approaches, Navi attempts to defend her wounded friend, but is pushed aside by the demon. <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= No more running! It's time for Navi to fight!... Yikes!|book= OoT (Himekawa)|volume= 2|publisher= |page= 94}}</ref> Luckily, Princess Zelda retrieves the [[Master Sword]], allowing Link to resume the fight. Navi alerts Link to Ganon's weak point, <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= His tail!! His tail is his weak point!!|book= OoT (Himekawa)|volume= 2|publisher= |page= 96}}</ref> allowing the hero to wound him.  At the end of the {{OoT (Himekawa)}}, just as Navi leaves Link, she tells him that she loves him, <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= Link... I love you!|book= OoT (Himekawa)|publisher= |page= 107}}</ref> and that the forest will be safe with a magnificent hero. <ref>{{Cite Book|quote= Link, you're a magnificent hero! The forest will be safe with you there.|book= OoT (Himekawa)|volume= 2|publisher= |page= 107}}</ref>
{{Noncanon|End}}

==Development==
When the concept of [[Targeting System|Z-targeting]] was being developed, an upside-down triangle was used to determine which enemy Link was targeting. The designers felt this marker was too simple, so they wanted to replace it with a cute Fairy girl, believing it would fit the ''Zelda'' atmosphere. However, the [[Nintendo 64]] was not able to support such a Fairy, so a ball of light with wings was used instead. She was originally called the "Fairy Navigation System," but was later simply named Navi. After naming her, many of her functions were designed, such as changing color to distinguish between friends and foes, acting as a guide, and providing strategy tips.

Her design also allowed developers to overcome a problem in [[Kokiri Forest]]. Due to the Nintendo 64's limitations, it was difficult to display the villagers and structures all at once, so each person was paired with a Fairy to help locate them. When Link approached them, their owners would appear and he could interact with them. Both of these expanded the story so that Link was the only child in the forest without a Fairy, then he met and parted with a Fairy companion.<ref>{{Cite Web|quote= |author= |published= |retrieved= |url= https://iwataasks.nintendo.com/interviews/3ds/zelda-ocarina-of-time/1/3|title= Iwata Asks: Ocarina of Time 3D Original Development Staff - Part 1|site= Official Nintendo website|type=}}</ref>

Navi was originally designed to be able to carry things for Link,<ref>{{Cite Person|quote= Press the B-Button, and you can speak with Navie. She can also carry things for Link.|name= Shigeru Miyamoto|url= http://www.ign.com/articles/1997/11/27/the-z-files-4|title= The Z-Files}}</ref> and turn red in the presence of danger.<ref>{{Cite Person|quote= Depending on the item, Navi will change to a different color. For example, she'll turn red if there's something dangerous, etc.|name= Shigeru Miyamoto|url= http://www.ign.com/articles/1997/11/27/the-z-files-4|title= The Z-Files}}</ref>

In a 1999 interview, [[Shigeru Miyamoto]] described Navi as "the biggest weak point" of {{OoT|-}}. Due to the difficulty of designing a system capable of tailoring advice to a player's situation, Navi was deliberately left "stupid" and repetitive. Miyamoto had wanted to remove the advice system entirely, but decided this would have been "even more unfriendly to players".<ref>{{Cite Person|quote= I think the whole system with Navi giving you advice is the biggest weakpoint of Ocarina of Time. It's incredibly difficult to design a system that gives proper advice, advice that's tailored to the player's situation. [...] If you read Navi's text, she says the same things over and over. I know it makes it sound bad, but we purposely left her at a kind of "stupid" level. [...] The truth is I wanted to remove the entire system, but that would have been even more unfriendly to players.|name= Shigeru Miyamoto|title= Ocarina of Time – 1999 Developer Interview|url= https://shmuplations.com/ocarinaoftime/|archive= |published= n.d.|retrieved= February 26, 2026}}</ref>

==Reception==
Navi is one of the more criticized {{TLoZ Series}} characters, which is due to her constant yelling of "Hey!" and "Listen!" throughout the game and for giving "unsolicited advice."<ref>{{Cite Web|quote= Before long, however, it became HEY! clear that she intended to be with LISTEN! us throughout the remainder of the game. And that might not have been so bad, except for her constant HEY! yammering. She also had a bad habit of interrupting our LISTEN! exploration by repeating the HEY! same all-text suggestions over and HEY! over, or floating above some HEY! object of interest that we either were LISTEN! already done with, or weren't ready to be interested LISTEN! in yet. But her unsolicited advice, interruptions and demands for attention would all have been tolerable if she hadn't insisted on driving us insane by repeatedly yelping the same two LISTEN! HEY! HEY! HEY! LISTEN! HEY! LISTEN! LISTEN! LISTEN! LISTEN! HEY! HEY! HEY! LISTEN! HEY! LISTEN! LISTEN! HEY! LISTEN! HEY! HEY! HEY! LISTEN! HEY! LISTEN! LISTEN! LISTEN! LISTEN! HEY! LISTEN! HEY! LISTEN! LISTEN! HEY! HEY! HEY! HEY! HEY! HEY! HEY! HEY! HEY! HEY! HEY! LISTEN! HEY! HEY! LISTEN! HEY! LISTEN! LISTEN! LISTEN! LISTEN! HEY! LISTEN! HEY! LISTEN! words. WHAT!?|title= The Top 7... Irritating female characters|url= http://www.gamesradar.com/f/the-top-7-irritating-female-characters/a-20080728104413532023/p-3|site= GamesRadar}}</ref><ref>{{Cite Web|quote= Anyone who has ever played this game should remember constantly hearing a tiny little voice saying: "Hey!...Hey!...Listen!...Hey!...Watch out!...Hey!..." SHUT [...] UP! I'm trying to have an adventure here.|title= The 15 Most Annoying Video Game Characters (From Otherwise Great Games)|url= http://www.cracked.com/article_15902_15-most-annoying-video-game-characters-from-otherwise-great-games.html|site= Cracked.com}}</ref> Cracked.com editor, Tim Lovett, listed Navi the eighth most annoying video character, mentioning how she "pester[ed]" Link like a "naggy, clinging spouse."<ref>{{Cite Web|quote= She shows how much she cares for Link by constantly pestering him like a nagging, clingy spouse.|title= The 15 Most Annoying Video Game Characters (From Otherwise Great Games)|url= http://www.cracked.com/article_15902_15-most-annoying-video-game-characters-from-otherwise-great-games.html|site= Cracked.com}}</ref> Although Mikel Reparaz from GamesRadar credited Navi for helping players by locking onto targets and enemies,<ref>{{Cite Web|quote= But we grudgingly put up with her presence, because she HEY! taught us how to get around in the LISTEN! world and helpfully floated above whatever objects or LISTEN! monsters we locked our HEY! aim onto.|title= The Top 7 Irritating female characters|url= http://www.gamesradar.com/f/the-top-7-irritating-female-characters/a-20080728104413532023/p-3|site= GamesRadar}}</ref> he criticized her for the overused "Hey! Listen!" phrase and listed her as the number one most irritating female character. Additionally, another GamesRadar editor ranked her second place in a list of "cutesy characters" they want to "beat the crap out of," describing her as a "tactless" {{wp|Tinkerbell}} and considering her to distract players from the gameplay.<ref>{{Cite Web|quote= You know why. Was there ever a more annoying sidekick/targeting reticule in the world? Sure, she was "cute" in that Tinkerbell sort of way - but Tink had class whereas Navi was utterly tactless. She led you off cliffs, distracted you from cool stuff. And she never, ever shut the hell up - even when we might have had a shot at finally getting to second base with Zelda.|title= Top 7 Cutesy Characters We Want to Beat the Crap Out Of|url= http://www.gamesradar.com/f/top-7-cutesy-characters-we-want-to-beat-the-crap-out-of/a-20080421104759115042/p-6|site= GamesRadar}}</ref> GameDaily also listed her as one of the gaming characters they "wish they could kill, but can't."<ref>{{Cite Web|quote= "Hey! Listen! Hey! Listen!" Unless you acknowledge this little fairy's existence, she'll continue to annoy both you and Link until you dream of drawing his Master Sword and cutting her wings off. We can't remember the number of times we fantasized about feeding her to a hungry skulltula. Alas, she's invincible and therefore, even more irritating.|title= Characters We Wish We Could Kill (But Can't)|url= http://web.archive.org/web/20090508073356/http://www.gamedaily.com/articles/galleries/characters-we-wish-we-could-kill-but-cant/?page=3&cp=2|site= GameDaily}}</ref>

==Trivia==
*In an interview with [[Shigeru Miyamoto]], he mentioned that Navi is jealous of Princess Zelda, as she feels something for Link.<ref>{{Cite Person|quote= However, this time Navie [the fairy] is jealous of Zelda. So within the story, Navie feels something for Link.|name= Shigeru Miyamoto|url= http://www.ign.com/articles/1997/12/04/the-z-files|title= The Z-Files}}</ref>
*Before {{BotW}}, Navi was one of the few characters with any voice acting in the series to use actual English words. During development of the [[The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2)|Nintendo Switch 2 remake of the original game]], the developers chose to do blind auditions for the voice actors so they would be forced to choose voices that were as close possible to the originals. Because of this, the original Japanese voice actor for Navi, [[Kaori Mizuhashi]], was chosen to reprise the role of Navi without the developers even realizing.<ref>{{Cite Person|quote= We deliberately hid the voice actors’ names during the Japanese auditions to force ourselves to decide based solely on which voices most closely resembled those of the original. And as fate would have it, one of the actors we selected had actually voiced the same character in the Nintendo 64 version. None of us saw that coming.|name= Eiji Aonuma|title= Ask the Developer Vol. 24: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — Part 4|url= https://www.nintendo.com/us/whatsnew/ask-the-developer-vol-24-the-legend-of-zelda-ocarina-of-time-part-4/|archive= |published= November 3, 2026|retrieved= November 7, 2026}}</ref>
*Navi appears as the guide of the Japanese {{OoT|-}} Official Guide Video, where she is fully voiced.<ref>{{Cite Web|quote= |author= Gamer Night Live|published= January 8, 2012|retrieved= |url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TLu5csyn3IQ|title= Ocarina of Time Japanese Promo|site= YouTube|type=}}</ref>
*Navi appears as a mouse cursor in the Japanese {{OoT3D}} website.<ref>[http://www.nintendo.co.jp/3ds/aqej/index.html {{OoT3D|-}} official Japanese website]</ref>
* In {{BotW|-}} and {{TotK}}, [[Nabi Lake]], [[South Nabi Lake]], the [[South Nabi Lake Well]], and [[East Batrea Lake|West Nabi Lake]] are all named after Navi.<ref>{{Cite Guide|BotW Piggyback|page= 351}}</ref>

==Nomenclature==
Navi's name comes from the word "navigation." Navi was originally supposed to be named "Fairy Navigation System," but since the name was too long, the developers changed it simply to Navi.<ref>{{Cite Person|quote= I called it the Fairy Navigation System, took it to Osawa-san, and asked, "How's this?" He immediately said, "Let's name it Navi." Because she navigates!|name= Yoshiaki Koizumi|url= https://iwataasks.nintendo.com/interviews/3ds/zelda-ocarina-of-time/1/3|title= Iwata Asks: Ocarina of Time 3D Original Development Staff - Part 1}}</ref>
